findings.reason: the same defect was raised against f-wftl-002 and answered by writing f-wftl-003 to name every unbuilt section; adding §20 without updating f-wftl-003 repeats it, and §20 would sit unbuilt behind a record that says the plan is fully queued.
findings.text: f-wftl-003, the plan's only open followup, is titled "Build §3, §6 to §19" and names §17, §18 and §19 as the unbuilt sections, but §20 is declared implementable and is named by no followup, so a coordinator driving the plan from its open followup never dispatches §20

findings.reason: a node that satisfies every clause of this section still refuses a §2-style landing on the control log, so the section delivers two of its three stated cases and the refusal it was written to remove survives.
findings.text: §17's Why gives three refusals it exists to end, and the first is §2's, refused because the guard read a repair round's control log that kept only its exit line while the run's first control log named both failing tests; the deliverable and done-when act only on baseline and after arms (missing, other revision, other command), so a node implementing §17 exactly leaves the control-log refusal in place and its gate cannot show it ended

findings.reason: the cited evidence names a mechanism outside the declared endpoint, so either the deliverable becomes wait-conditioned under a truthful declaration or the plan carries a stated cause its scope does not act on.
findings.text: the section argues from three refusals that "every one of this plan's first landings was refused on how a suite arm or control was recorded", yet its endpoint is stated over suite arms alone, and the control log is a distinct manifest field read by the landing guard (reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py:1933, reckon/crew/promotion_records.py:327), so the reasoning that motivates the section does not carry through to what it declares done
